adoption.notes: The signer names the producer half of this contract from c525f53, which merged the module unused; the claim qualifies at 95a08b7, which wired it into command egress. Runtime liveness signing is labelled Partial in the runtime capability matrix.

Its headers cite this contract as the source of what they verify; none states conformance. Its liveness verifier implements runtime liveness, which v1's baseline audit moved to firmware-commands/v2. Its liveness corpus generator, test/golden/generate_liveness_vectors.py, still names firmware-commands/v1.md#runtime-liveness in the corpus it writes; it reproduces firmware-commands/liveness-at-v-1-vectors-v2.json once that member names firmware-commands/v2.md#runtime-liveness, a change that lands with its next re-vendor.

hunks.summary: The `ori/fw/<device_id>/runtime` topic row: a liveness message that only the Runtime Liveness section defines. Restored in v1.

The retained approval authorizes the runtime command key only; MQTT certificate operations are firmware-mqtt-provisioning/v1's. v1's approval grammar cannot carry a certificate operation, so no accepted input changes.
Pointer: when an approval may be issued and published is normative in device-provisioning/v1, which binds the same parties.
The Runtime Liveness section: a fixed grammar, device-side refusals, freshness, expiry, timing and its corpus. Restored in v1.
The runtime obligations to publish liveness, observe the supervision window and persist runtime_seq. Restored in v1.
The required artifacts: provisioning-approval vector sets and the runtime liveness artifact list. Restored in v1.
